title: Why Earning More Still Keeps You Broke (The Diderot Trap)
alt_title_2: Why High Earners Still Live Paycheck to Paycheck
description_hook: In 1769 the philosopher Denis Diderot was given a scarlet robe, and it made everything else he owned look shabby. This video shows how the Diderot Effect drains modern paychecks, and a simple rule to stop it. Stat: PYMNTS Intelligence, Jan 2024.

scenes.headline: Why Getting a Raise Makes People Poorer
scenes.stat_label: OF $100K+ EARNERS LIVE PAYCHECK TO PAYCHECK
bullets: Higher income rarely fixes money stress
A 250-year-old psychological chain reaction explains why
scenes.narration: Nearly half of Americans earning over one hundred thousand dollars a year live paycheck to paycheck. A story from 1769 explains why.

scenes.headline: Denis Diderot & The Scarlet Robe (1769)
bullets: Gifted one luxury scarlet dressing gown
Suddenly his desk, rug, and chairs looked 'cheap'
scenes.narration: In 1769, the philosopher Denis Diderot wrote about a luxurious scarlet robe he had been given. Next to that robe, his old desk looked cheap. So he replaced the desk. Then the tapestry. Then the chairs.
scenes.source: Denis Diderot, 'Regrets on Parting with My Old Dressing Gown' (1769)

scenes.headline: One Upgrade Triggers Five Hidden Costs
scenes.left_body: New phone -> watch -> earbuds -> monthly subscriptions
scenes.right_body: Freeze lifestyle for 12 months after every raise
scenes.narration: The anthropologist Grant McCracken later named this the Diderot Effect. You rarely buy just one upgrade. You buy a new identity that demands more purchases to match.

scenes.headline: The 50% Invisible Raise Rule
scenes.stat_subtext: Lifestyle still grows, margin compounds 4x faster
scenes.narration: To break the spiral, use the Invisible Raise Rule: whenever your income jumps, automatically route fifty percent into assets before it ever hits your checking account.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)

scenes.headline: Wealth Is What You Don't Spend
bullets: Wait 72 hours before matching a new purchase
Keep the raise, skip the chain reaction
scenes.narration: Real wealth isn't what people see in your driveway, it's the freedom you didn't trade away.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
